During the 2025 summer transfer window, Liverpool broke the bank, spending £410m.

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz were the two most expensive signings, as the Swedish striker arrived for £123m (€145m) and the German attacking midfielder for £106m (€125m). But for many months, the two most expensive recruits in the club's history failed to live up to expectations.

According to recent reports, in his first season at Liverpool, Wirtz scored seven goals and provided 10 assists in 49 games, but his impact was largely disappointing. Isak, for his part, barely played (four goals and one assist in 22 games) because of a fractured fibula. That summer 2025 transfer window was thus described as 'the worst transfer window in Premier League history'.

Both attackers were therefore expected to deliver in their second season at Liverpool, with fresh manager Andoni Iraola arriving.

The momentum is completely different at the start of this campaign, as the 3-0 win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night in the Champions League illustrated perfectly. Isak scored twice, while Wirtz also found the net.

The Swede is rediscovering the efficiency that made his reputation at Newcastle United. He now has ten goals in all competitions in 16 games and has just scored in six consecutive away games for Liverpool. The 27-year-old is establishing himself as the number nine Liverpool had long been waiting for.

On Wednesday night, Isak was asked about when he would be back at his best level: 'It is always difficult to say, but I can definitely say that I feel good, the team is in a good rhythm, that is the most notable thing' - he mentioned.

After a season of adaptation to English football, in which he struggled to have an impact in the final third and to be decisive, Wirtz is in excellent form.

Still deployed as a number 10, the 23-year-old German has scored four goals and provided five assists in 17 games in all competitions for Liverpool.

Sources indicate that his November has been excellent: three goals and two assists in three games for Liverpool, as well as three goals in two games for the German national team. Wirtz appears to have digested his huge transfer and to be ready to shed his 'flop' label at Liverpool.

  • Winless against Lorient in two years, Paris Saint-Germain welcome the 10th-placed visitors to Parc des Princes for Saturday's matchday 12 clash.
  • The defending Ligue 1 champions' 12-match winning streak was halted by Roma on Wednesday, but they now aim to extend their sequence of eight consecutive top-flight victories.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 09:45.

Winless against Lorient in two years, Paris Saint-Germain welcome the 10th-placed visitors to Parc des Princes for Saturday's matchday 12 clash.

The defending Ligue 1 champions' 12-match winning streak was halted by Roma on Wednesday, but they now aim to extend their sequence of eight consecutive top-flight victories.

PSG had maintained a perfect record across all competitions for nearly three months before Roma visited in the Champions League in midweek, with the Serie A side battling to a 2-2 draw on matchday five.

That result ended the Parisians' four-match European winning streak, although Luis Enrique's men remain second in the league-phase standings and firmly inside the coveted top-eight places that guarantee last-16 qualification.

Returning to league action should please supporters, who have watched their side claim eight consecutive victories since losing to Monaco at the start of September, albeit with only three clean sheets.

However, eagle-eyed observers will note that the Red and Blues have won only one of their last five meetings with Lorient across the past four years, with three of the last four encounters ending level.

Another draw would please Paris FC, Lille and Lyon, who trail the capital club by three, five and six points respectively as the Ligue 1 title race begins to take shape.

Alexandre Dujeux therefore aims to prevent Lorient's first defeat in this fixture since April 2024; however, his own five-match winless record against PSG and four consecutive losses to Enrique are ominous signs for the 50-year-old manager.

An indifferent run of results further undermines confidence in Les Merlus extending their unbeaten sequence in this fixture, with the Brittany-based club winning only one of their last four league matches.

Admittedly, only one of those matches ended in defeat, a 2-0 home loss to Brest, while their solitary victory during that period came away at Le Havre.

However, that early-November success offers limited encouragement given that it came against the division's bottom side, who have collected a paltry two points from 11 matches.

Their overall away record is more encouraging, with Dujeux's team conceding just twice across five matches on the road, both in September's 2-1 defeat to Le Mans, while keeping clean sheets in the other four.

Another shutout would make Lorient the first team since Monaco in November last year to prevent PSG from scoring, a feat far easier said than done.

Paris Saint-Germain Ligue 1 form:.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue are both sidelined with ACL injuries for PSG's fixture on Saturday.

Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos are pushing for their first starts since last month's 4-2 victory over Barcelona, although Enrique may be tempted to retain the centre-back partnership of Ilya Zabarnyi and Willian Pacho.

Ferran Torres remains the capital club's leading Ligue 1 scorer with five goals, while Achraf Hakimi, Senny Mayulu and Marquinhos have three apiece.

Lorient have shared the goals around this season, with nine different players finding the net for the Brittany-based visitors.

Only Jean-Victor Makengo has scored more than once for Les Merlus, leaving Dujeux searching for someone to step up at Parc des Princes.

The visitors' prospects are further weakened by the absence of Panos Katseris, with a muscle injury ruling their leading goal provider out of this weekend's encounter.

Isaak Toure (groin) and Bandiougou Fadiga (muscle) are also sidelined for the 10th-placed side on matchday 12.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:.

Safonov; Hakimi, Pacho, Marquinhos, Mendes; Zaire-Emery, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Dembele, Godts.

Lorient possible starting lineup:.

Mvogo; Adjei, Talbi, Obaretin; Sylla, Cadiou, Ebong, Kouassi; Makengo, Bernardeau; Tosin.

Lorient's four clean sheets from five away matches suggest that PSG may need patience, particularly against opponents who have repeatedly frustrated them in recent meetings.

However, the visitors' limited scoring threat and Katseris's absence should allow Enrique's men to sustain pressure and eventually secure a ninth consecutive league victory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan have four games left to play in the Europa League and they’re in the do-or-die stage of the competition already.

Thoughts on the Europa League this season were mixed. On paper, Milan should have been competing at the top. Yet, they’ve struggled through the League Phase so far, leaving themselves with something of a mountain to climb, starting against Olympiacos later this week.

Recent findings suggest that as Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the Rossoneri are in a more-than-difficult position. Sitting 28th in the rankings, they are right now outside the qualification spots and calculations are difficult to make about how much they’ll need to improve.

According to recent reports, from the past two seasons, they’ll need between 14 and 16 points to qualify for the top eight, which feels like a distant hope. If they’re to achieve that amount, they must win all four of their remaining games and hope that 15 is enough.

Daily briefing: Is AI ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’?

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Depending on whom you ask, OpenAI’s huge drop of AI-generated proofs last month was either an unprecedented achievement or a catastrophe — or both.
  • Amateur astronomers are turning to AI models to search for worlds outside the Solar System.
  • A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people’s brains identified molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Depending on whom you ask, OpenAI’s huge drop of AI-generated proofs last month was either an unprecedented achievement or a catastrophe — or both. “It’s probably the end of mathematics as we know it,” theoretical physicist Miranda Cheng said at an emergency meeting of the Royal Society. Now Anthropic has claimed a full proof of the iconic Riemann hypothesis. Mathematicians are grappling with what might come next — and say that the field’s tradition of openly sharing early ideas is already coming to an end.

Amateur astronomers are turning to AI models to search for worlds outside the Solar System. AI’s ability to scour the internet for freely available planet-hunting tools, such as those made by NASA, and use them to process massive amounts of data has lowered the barrier to entry for non-specialists, researchers say. But some citizen scientists don’t fully understand how to validate the findings of AI models, states exoplanet researcher Michelle Kunimoto. “There’s been a huge, overwhelming surge of AI-driven papers” that describe relatively low-quality planet candidates, they say.

Reference: Zenodo preprint (not peer reviewed).

A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people’s brains identified molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These changes include ‘epigenetic marks’ — chemical tags added to DNA that can affect how genes work. And some patterns occurred only in women. Understanding the epigenetic consequences of trauma could help to explain why some people experience symptoms and respond to treatment differently.

According to recent reports, pakistani military pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali is set to become the first foreign astronaut to visit China’s Tiangong space station. Ali is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese taikonauts. “My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters at a press conference. The mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme, which now has the capability to offer such opportunities to international partners, says foreign-policy researcher Yuxuan Jia.

In Six Maths Essentials, Fields medallist Terence Tao explains how an understanding of the central principles of mathematics can help us to understand the world — all in fewer than 100 pages. For Tao, these six concepts — numbers, algebra, geometry, probability, analysis and dynamics — are the building blocks of reality, and he describes each principle “with elegant minimalism”, writes biomedical scientist Itai Yanai in his review. “The beauty of Tao’s book is seeing maths through his eyes, describing its spirit as well as generalizing across the discipline.”.

Sources indicate that biomedical-ethics researcher Brandon Brown argues that if scientists want to advance in their careers, it’s their own responsibility to make peers aware of their achievements. A panel of Nature readers gave their judgement — read on to see if you agree.

In a recent development, scientific techniques used to investigate the provenance of historical artefacts also shed light on what early chemists knew. Some analyses of art from 18th-century Saxon and Qing dynasties say that they’re later replicas, because the cobalt pigments are too pure — people didn’t know how to eliminate nickel so thoroughly until much later. But not so fast, write five archaeological scientists. They’ve spotted evidence from a European pigment factory as far back as 1731 that might be “the earliest documented protocol for the selective wet chemical separation of chemically similar elements”. Give these ‘chymists’ from artisanal workshops their due, say the authors.

Sources indicate that rich countries that invest in weather-monitoring stations in places that can’t afford their own will reap the benefits of better forecasts and early warning systems, argues Markus Repnik, a director of a United Nations fund called the Systematic Observations Financing Facility (SOFF). (Nature | 7 min read).

Reference: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and World Meteorological Organization report for SOFF.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03841-2.

Today I might go birding, right after I steal some cars. But don’t worry: both will take place in the open world of video game Grand Theft Auto VI. As well as all kinds of shenanigans that would be illegal in the real world, players can spot some 60 bird species, along with reptiles, amphibians, fish and mammals.

Flora Graham, chief editor, Nature Briefing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 26 Nov 2026 10:16.

Former Manchester United star Gordon Strachan - speaking exclusively to Sports Mole - has urged the Red Devils to sign a £62.8m midfielder to help correct their "phenomenal" transfer mistakes.

Upcoming Man Utd manager Mauricio Pochettino remains winless since replacing Michael Carrick following Wednesday's infuriating 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League, in which the Red Devils fell behind, took the lead and were then pegged back in Portugal.

The four-goal stalemate marked the seventh game in a row that Man United had conceded at least two goals, and once again, the Red Devils' open midfield was exposed.

The pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo did not cover themselves in glory against Liverpool or Sporting, and the former is now suspended for RB Leipzig in December after being sent off towards the end of Wednesday's game.

Andrey Santos has also not yet had the desired impact since joining from Chelsea, while fellow 22-year-old Carlos Baleba has played just 397 minutes across seven appearances due to injury problems.

Speaking to Sports Mole via William Hill betting site, Strachan - who scored 36 goals in 198 games for Man United - has told the Red Devils hierarchy to make a move for Crystal Palace lynchpin Adam Wharton to help offset the "phenomenal" amount of money the club has wasted on under-performing players.

In a recent development, "Adam Wharton is one of my picks," Strachan noted. "Elliot Anderson was also another one they should have gone for. Tielemans has been doing well in the Premier League for nearly 10 years, so they're buying somebody who's at the latter stage of his career. I might be wrong, I hope I'm wrong, and hopefully, he’s got another five or six years in him.

"And I've got to say, the world of football in England is full of the top teams, especially Chelsea, Spurs, bringing in players who sign for £40m, £50m, you go, who is he? There's just so many players like this now.

"You see some of these players, and you go, what has he done to deserve a £45m fee? Baleba, Santos, you’re picking up people for substantial fees, who have no reputation.

"Who's been brave here? Is this just a kind of cosy midfield? You could go back to Mason Mount for £40m - who actually signed this off to pay this amount of money for players?

It has been revealed that "It’s just beyond belief the money that Man United have wasted. It's phenomenal. And that's from the recruitment not doing their work properly.

Industry observers note that "They've got to start saying, what is my plan for the next 10 years at Man United? And how do we go about this? Arsenal were a bit like that five or six years ago. It wasn't anywhere near as bad a situation as Man United, but they stuck to their plan, and it paid off.".

Data from the 2026-27 season does not paint Wharton in the most positive light compared to his Man United peers, given Crystal Palace's atrocious start to the campaign.

Indeed, the England international only leads Baleba, Tielemans, Santos and Mainoo on games played, crosses per 90 and accurate crosses per 90, while also winning the fewest duels and registering the lowest percentage of successful passes.

However, Wharton has committed the fewest fouls per 90 minutes of the quintet, and he has been dispossessed on the second-fewest occasions per 90 minutes, only behind Santos.

Thanks to Crystal Palace's perilous position in the Premier League table - Thomas Frank's men sit bottom of the rankings with just seven points from nine games - interested parties could pick up Wharton for a discount if the Eagles are relegated to the Championship.

The 22-year-old is valued at €75m (£62.8m) by Transfermarkt and has three years left on his Palace contract, but Man United may have to fend off competition from Liverpool and Chelsea to land him in 2027.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 10:27.

Bournemouth have prepared for their Europa League clash at Celta Vigo in the knowledge that they could smash even more history.

Marco Rose's side won just two of their opening eight competitive matches of the 2026-27 season, hinting that there could be a period of struggle following Andoni Iraola's departure to Liverpool.

However, with the Cherries set for a Celta Vigo challenge on Thursday night, it is clear that the Dean Court club are thriving, with the visitors to Spain sitting in fifth position in the Premier League standings.

A star of the current positive form, Evanilson has truly announced himself as an elite top-flight striker, netting seven goals and providing two assists in his past eight appearances, scoring in five consecutive league fixtures.

What makes Bournemouth's run even more impressive is that last season's star man Junior Kroupi has barely started a competitive match so far after recovering from a broken leg sustained over the summer.

Starting with a 3-0 Europa League success over Austrian side Sturm Graz on October 15, Bournemouth have recorded nine straight victories in all competitions across the Premier League, EFL Cup and European action.

That winning streak is the longest since the Cherries became a Football League club at the beginning of the 1923-24 season, showcasing how impressively the South Coast team are performing at the moment.

However, there are still more records to be achieved over the coming weeks, with Bournemouth aiming to become only the eighth team to record 10 straight competitive victories whilst playing in the Premier League.

Winning the Premier League during the 2016-17 campaign under Antonio Conte, Chelsea managed 10 wins in a row in all competitions, with that particular streak running from October 2016 until Latest Year's Eve 2016.

Leeds are the other club to post that exact number of wins in succession, with the Elland Road side completing the feat between August and October during the 1999-00 Premier League term.

The dominant force in English domestic football during the late 2010s and early 2020s, Manchester City are unsurprisingly the club with the most consecutive competitive wins as a Premier League side.

Under the expert stewardship of Pep Guardiola, the title-winning Citizens won 21 straight matches between December 2020 and March 2021, destroying Arsenal's previous record of 13 games in succession.

To match Man City's record, Bournemouth would need to secure victory in Spain on Thursday before winning every single match up to and including the trip to Brighton & Hove Albion on January 5.

Alexander Isak is now into double digits for goals for Liverpool this season, having netted twice in the 3-0 victory away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds’ record signing endured a tough first campaign at Anfield after his £125m move from Newcastle, scoring just four times and being sidelined for four months due to a broken leg.

Those initial struggles now seem like a distant memory after his brace in Belgium tonight took him onto 10 goals in 16 matches for his club in 2026/27, already more than doubling his tally from the whole of last term.

Isak opened the scoring for Liverpool in the first half at the Jan Breydel Stadium and wrapped up the victory in the 83rd minute by outmuscling Brandon Mechele, advancing into the penalty area and coolly lofting the ball over Yann Sommer in the Club Brugge net.

According to recent reports, calling that goal for TNT Sports, Sam Matterface gushed: “That’s brilliant from Isak. He’s got away from Mechele and he’s bursting into the box, and this will seal it…oh, it’s beautiful, delicious! Such a brilliant finish.”.

It has been revealed that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Recent findings suggest that the manner in which Isak took that clinching goal shows just how much confidence is flowing through his veins right now. Every time he gets the ball in that area of the pitch, he looks like finishing off the chance (aside from an uncharacteric miss against Manchester United on Sunday).

It isn’t just the quality of his finishing which is standing out, either – as Ian Doyle noted for the Liverpool Echo, the 27-year-old helped to create his first goal by pressing the Club Brugge defence and forcing the error from Sommer.

He also looks increasingly at ease with his fellow attackers, with a neat chemistry now forming on the pitch, and his confidence is evident in how he runs at opposition defences with an attitude of “I’ve got you!”.

John Aldridge recently claimed that Isak may well be targeting somewhere in the region of 20 to 25 goals for the season, and the Swede is already halfway to the lower end of that bracket with one more match still to play in November.

Along with fellow 2025 arrival Florian Wirtz, Liverpool’s number 9 is showing everyone why his current club spent such a vast money on him.

If he doesn’t suffer a recurrence of the injury problems which ruined his first campaign with the Reds, he could easily end up hitting or even surpassing the target that Aldridge has set.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Published: 12:01 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Given how swiftly things have unravelled under Sebastien Pocognoli, serious questions are now being asked of those in power at the Scottish Football Association.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 24 November 2026.

Given how swiftly things have unravelled under Sebastien Pocognoli, serious questions are now being asked of those in power at the Scottish Football Association.

Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the chief executive and chief football officer who led the recruitment process, certainly talked a good game when Pocognoli was appointed.

However, when Mulholland took up his position in the summer, his remit was much broader than merely the appointment of a newly introduced head coach for the national team. He was tasked with trying to initiate a much-needed revamp of youth development throughout Scottish football.

Only a few months into the job, those plans have already hit the buffers due to resistance from clubs, despite the obvious need for more young Scottish players to play more first-team football.

The SFA had proposed including two Under-21 players starting in cup competitions and the same age group playing a minimum of 6 per cent of all available minutes across a season in league competition.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland has met resistance in his bid to shake up the game.

When it immediately became clear that several clubs in Scotland weren’t keen on that, a newly introduced watered-down version was then put back on the table.

Now there have been reports that those plans might be booted even further into the long grass and possibly won’t even be voted on at all this season.

As is always the case, the self-serving interest from clubs in Scotland will always trump the need for national reform.

According to recent reports, but that is only part of the story. What is also of serious concern is the lack of quality coaching afforded to players in academies across the country.

If that was to be addressed, clubs would perhaps feel more obliged to play more younger players if they were ready for first-team football.

Industry observers note that it is a multi-faceted problem – and one which Mulholland is no closer to solving. Clubs are selfish and will serve their own needs, with no obligation to buy into any newly introduced proposals.

Sources indicate that the SFA could stand firm and try to force some of these looks through as non-negotiable. A tough stance, albeit one that risks becoming messy.

But nobody should be naïve enough to believe that self-interest from the clubs is the root of all problems here. It is much, much deeper than that.

  • Jack Wilshere's side will be looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions after coming from behind to win 2-1 last weekend, while Aaron Ramsey and his U's will be aiming to move into the automatic promotion places by securing a fourth win in five third-tier outings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 10:55, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:05.

Two former Arsenal teammates come head to head on Saturday in League One as in-form Luton Town welcome high-flying Oxford United to Kenilworth Road.

Jack Wilshere's side will be looking to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches in all competitions after coming from behind to win 2-1 last weekend, while Aaron Ramsey and his U's will be aiming to move into the automatic promotion places by securing a fourth win in five third-tier outings.

More than six months after Luton Town narrowly missed out on a place in the League One playoffs last season, finishing just one point behind sixth-placed Leyton Orient, the Hatters have made a positive start to the 2026-27 campaign as they look to go one step better this time around.

Wilshere's side began the new season inconsistently and were sitting 16th after seven third-tier matches at the end of September, but have since enjoyed an impressive upturn in form, losing just once in the league across October and November, a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons at Stadium MK.

That run has seen Luton win six of their last eight league matches, while also progressing to the second round of the FA Cup and the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy, putting them firmly back in the playoff picture.

In fact, the Hatters could move into second place heading into the final month of the calendar year if they secure a ninth league victory of the season and other results go their way this weekend, with their recent form having lifted them more than 10 places into fifth and guaranteed them a place in the top six until at least their 17th league match next week, when they face struggling Blackpool.

A key factor behind their turnaround has been an improvement in front of goal, with Luton scoring 17 times in League One since the start of October, an average of more than two per game that has taken their overall tally to 29, a record bettered by just one side in the division.

As for the visitors, Oxford United make the 66-mile journey to Bedfordshire in similarly strong form and will be looking to move into December in the top two by recording a third consecutive victory.

The U's, led by former Wales midfielder Ramsey, have enjoyed a more consistent campaign than their upcoming opponents, having already moved into the top six by their seventh match of the 2026-27 season, when Luton were sitting 16th, and have continued to build on that strong start in recent weeks to climb to third.

Oxford head into their 15th league outing of the season with 29 points following eight wins, five draws and just one defeat, and they could move level on points with leaders Stockport County this weekend while still having two games in hand on Jimmy McNulty's side.

Although Oxford's FA Cup campaign came to an end at the first hurdle with a 1-0 home defeat to Stevenage, their form in the third tier has been exceptional, with no side in the top four divisions of English football losing fewer league matches than the U's.

Only Ramsey and Wilshere's former club Arsenal and League Two side Barnet have matched their tally of just one defeat.

While Luton have built their campaign around a clinical attacking unit, Oxford's promotion push has been underpinned by a strong defensive record, with only three sides in League One having conceded fewer than their 14 goals.

However, shipping three at home to Wycombe Wanderers last weekend, despite coming from three goals behind to secure a remarkable 4-3 victory, represented a rare blemish on an otherwise impressive defensive campaign.

The pair meet for the first time in just under two years on Saturday and will lock horns in a third-tier fixture for the first time since 2019, with Luton having enjoyed a spell in the Premier League since their previous meeting at this level.

Oxford United form (all competitions):.

Luton Town will be forced into at least one change following their weekend victory over Burton Albion after Jordan Clark was forced off with an injury in the 33rd minute, with the midfielder expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Daniel Gore.

Clark is set to join fellow injury absentees Hakeem Odoffin, Gideon Kodua and Shayden Morris in the treatment room, with the latter yet to feature at all this season.

Former Bristol City forward Nahki Wells marked his 15th league appearance of the campaign with his eighth and ninth goals of the season, scoring a brace against the Brewers last Saturday, and the Bermudian is expected to lead the line once again.

Having been in EFL Trophy action during the week, beating Tottenham Hotspur Under-21s 2-1, Ramsey is expected to make wholesale changes for Oxford's return to League One action.

Jamie Cumming started in goal for the midweek cup tie and could retain his place ahead of Simon Eastwood, who conceded three times last weekend, while changes are also expected throughout the defence, midfield and attack.

Gatlin O'Donkor came off the bench to score a dramatic winner five minutes into stoppage time against Wycombe and could therefore be rewarded with a starting place on Saturday, potentially at the expense of Tyler Goodrham.

Shea; Jones, Mengi, Andersen, Johnston; Walsh; Richards, Donley, Gore, Palmer; Wells.

While Oxford United arrive at Kenilworth Road in high spirits, they face a side who have collected more points than any other team in the division across their last six league games, meaning the U's will know they face a difficult task to win at a ground where they have not tasted victory since 2017.

With that noted, Oxford did manage to come away from their last visit to Luton with a point, albeit more than two years ago, and we expect them to repeat that feat, with the two in form sides playing out a 2-2 draw.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola has shared an patch on the injury sustained by Victor Munoz in Liverpool’s win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The only blemish on a terrific result for the Reds in Belgium was the sight of the Spanish winger hobbling off towards the end of the first half, appearing to hurt his knee when overstretching to try and keep the ball after a surging run into the hosts’ penalty area.

A stretcher had been readied for the 23-year-old, but he was at least able to pick himself up off the ground and leave the pitch flanked by medical staff.

Speaking to reporters after the match, Iraola gave an patch on Munoz’s injury, with Liverpool’s number 23 due to go for an assessment to verify the seriousness of the issue.

It has been revealed that the Reds’ head coach stated (via liverpoolfc.com): “It is the worst part of the game, definitely. He was in a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game had finished.

“It has been a knock on the knee, so now we have to assess him. Then if he presents well tomorrow and it’s just this knock… but obviously it’s very early to tell if there is something more than the knock.

“In the moment it was very, very painful. After the game, I talked to him and he was a little bit more optimistic.”.

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The initial signs from Munoz certainly weren’t good, with the winger on the ground for a few minutes before managing to pick himself up, but this update from Iraola at least paints a slightly better picture for now.

We still have to wait for the outcome of the assessment that he’s due to undergo today before we know how severe the injury is, and how long he’s expected to be out of action.

We can only hope that it isn’t a serious setback for the 23-year-old, who’s looked bright and effervescent in his performances for Liverpool so far and was rewarded with a rare start last night before the unfortunate body blow.

Munoz had been playing well in Brugge, too, with Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle noting how the Spaniard offered a ‘real threat with his pace and a regular outlet down the right’ until he was forced off in the 42nd minute.

Fingers crossed for good news on the winger once the medical assessment is completed.

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 10:58.

Nice return to Ligue 1 action a week after Paris Saint-Germain ended their three-match winning streak, with promoted Troyes visiting Allianz Riviera on matchday 12.

The Europe-chasing hosts remain one of the division's form teams and will back themselves to overcome a promoted side they have beaten in their last three meetings.

Olivier Pantaloni and his players faced a formidable challenge against PSG last weekend, with the defending Ligue 1 champions arriving on a seven-match winning streak.

While PSG extended their sequence of top-flight victories to eight, Nice's three-match winning run ended against the Parisians, hardly a disgrace given their opponents' quality and form.

Les Aiglons remain one of Ligue 1's form teams, with their 12 points from the last available 18 surpassed by only three clubs: PSG (18), Marseille (15) and Brest (13).

Back at home just days after PSG ended their eight-month unbeaten run on their own turf, Pantaloni's men will target maximum points to reclaim a European place, with sixth-placed Brest and fifth-placed Marseille sitting one and two points above Nice respectively.

That ambition appears reasonable given the Eaglets' three consecutive victories in this fixture and four wins in the last five meetings, with the visitors needing a strong performance to beat Nice at Allianz Riviera for the first time since 2017.

Stephane Dumont's men will fancy their chances of a positive result as they enter matchday 12 having collected six points from the last available nine.

Their only defeat during that period was an understandable 1-0 reverse at PSG, a performance that offered ESTAC encouragement in their bid to avoid an immediate return to Ligue 2.

Troyes' recent improvement follows a six-match winless run that included five consecutive defeats, with last season's Ligue 2 champions failing to score in four of those losses.

Collecting six points from their recent fixtures has lifted them out of the relegation zone and into 14th, although Dumont's men sit just one point above Strasbourg in the relegation playoff spot and three clear of second-bottom Angers.

While a disastrous weekend could leave the top-flight returnees in the bottom three, that would require victories for Auxerre, Strasbourg and Angers, with the latter also needing a six-goal swing.

Mohamed Abdelmonem (hamstring) and Elye Wahi are doubtful, although the six-goal forward is expected to feature for the hosts this weekend.

Laurent Abergel and Antoine Mendy remain unavailable due to long-term knee injuries, while Moise Bombito is also sidelined with a leg problem.

Beyond Wahi, Jonathan Clauss (three goals, three assists), Mohamed Amoura (three goals, two assists) and Sofiane Diop (two goals, three assists) all possess match-winning quality for the Eaglets.

Troyes' leading attacking threats are last weekend's two-goal hero Antoine Mille and Renaud Ripart, who remain the visitors' only players to have scored more than once in 2026-27.

Merwan Ifnaoui faces a pre-match assessment to determine his availability this weekend, while Paolo Gozzi (hamstring) and Yacouba Kone (knee) are sidelined.

Diouf; Seidu, Ndayishimiye, Mandza; Clauss, Witsel, Boudaoui, Nkounkou; Diop, Amoura; Wahi.

Troyes possible starting lineup:.

Konate; Maronnier, Monfray, Diaz, Boura; Ifnaoui, Diop, Mille, Karim, Diawara; Ripart.

Troyes' six-point return from their last three matches and narrow defeat at PSG suggest that Nice should expect a more demanding assignment than the visitors' promoted status might imply.

However, the Eaglets have several reliable attacking contributors and have our backing to respond to last weekend's setback with a fourth consecutive victory in this fixture.

Francesco Camarda has spoken about his Champions League goal that never was today, and how it was an AC Milan dream come true.

Camarda first became known to Milan as a youngster, but he confirmed himself further when he became Serie A’s youngest-ever appearance maker. He almost then went to a European level, with a goal in the Champions League. However, it wasn’t to be.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, on his debut in the competition, the starlet bagged a goal which would’ve made him the Rossoneri’s youngest-ever scorer in Europe’s main stage. Yet it was ruled out for offside and a few years on, the now 18-year-old is still waiting for a first competitive goal for the Diavolo.

Speaking to Vice, the striker opened up about his dream of playing in the Champions League at San Siro, his emotions after his goal (and it later being disallowed) and how his teammates rallied around him, as MilanVibes relayed.

In a recent development, “As a child, I used to say to my dad: imagine if one day I could walk into San Siro and hear the Champions League anthem, accompanied by the roar of the entire stadium. When it actually happened, I thought back to that little boy and realised I had realised a dream.

It has been revealed that “When I stepped onto the pitch, I had an incredible adrenaline rush. Then the goal came, and I felt the whole stadium explode. I also felt the affection of my teammates, who immediately raised me into the air.

“However, when I looked at the scoreboard and saw that the VAR check was in progress, I was already convinced the goal would be disallowed.

It has been revealed that “When I returned home that evening, with my parents and cousin, I burst into tears. I was overjoyed by the goal, but at the same time deeply disappointed by what had happened. It wasn’t easy at first, but I also worked on my mental health and managed to put that moment behind me.

“Today, I’m proud of the journey I’ve taken and of having overcome those difficulties.”.

Sources indicate that “I remember what Gabbia told me: he was sorry for what happened, but he explained that the experience should give me even more motivation. It should push me to improve, to train harder, and to work so I can relive even more wonderful emotions.”.

In a recent development, “In football, there are positive and negative opinions; it has always been this way and will continue to be this way. A player’s true strength lies in not being influenced by what is remarked, because, regardless of whether you do well or badly, someone will always find a reason to judge you.”.

Industry News: Blend public cash and private innovation to unlock drug development

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1770 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh model of research and development is needed to incentivize manufacturers to go after diseases that aren’t sure bets.Credit: Stanislav Gvozd/Getty.
  • In a recent development, for decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation.
  • According to recent reports, this approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh model of research and development is needed to incentivize manufacturers to go after diseases that aren’t sure bets.Credit: Stanislav Gvozd/Getty.

In a recent development, for decades, most countries have followed the same model of biomedical innovation. Basic research is undertaken mostly by universities and academia, and private industry leads the translation of research into health solutions1.

According to recent reports, this approach has generated extraordinary drugs and therapies as well as economic success. In 2022, the pharmaceutical sector contributed US$2.3 trillion — or around 1.7% — to global gross domestic product (GDP) and supported 75 million jobs2.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science.

Recent findings suggest that however, market failures have been common. Companies have underinvested in developing therapeutics for common diseases with poorly understood biological mechanisms, such as depression, anxiety and kidney disease, because they consider them too commercially risky or unprofitable to pursue3.

To address this gap, we propose an adapted innovation model based on mission-driven public–private partnerships (PPPs), in which government acts as a leading strategic investor. By bringing together the best scientists in academia and industry and lowering risks in industry development in areas of public need and for diseases with limited understanding, this model would accelerate translation, advance health and increase economic returns.

In a recent development, here, we outline how it would work. It will require systems to ensure affordable access to drugs and therapies, as well as revenue sharing between public and private partners to guarantee public benefits and to support investments in innovation.

Complex diseases that affect swathes of the population create persistent health and economic burdens. Yet, the current biomedical innovation model has proved limited in addressing evolving health needs. Because private investment is guided by assessments of risk and return, it tends to favour diseases with well-defined biological mechanisms and high commercial potential. Diseases that are biologically complex, varied or associated with uncertain markets remain underexplored.

Recent findings suggest that for example, in 2023, more than 300 million people globally had depression. The condition will cost the global economy an estimated $12 trillion between 2025 and 20504. In the United States in 2024, one in five people reported that they had received a diagnosis of major depressive disorder during their lifetime, resulting in an economic burden of $334 billion annually across health-care, household-related and workforce costs5. Yet, the leading drug class for depression (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) has remained unchanged since the 1970s6.

The grand proposal to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

The grand plan to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care.

Recent findings suggest that other chronic diseases impose similarly large burdens. For example, chronic kidney disease affects around 800 million people worldwide — nearly one in seven — and is projected to become the fifth leading cause of death globally by 2040 if current trends continue7,8. Yet, existing therapies cannot stem its toll on human lives.

Antimicrobial resistance is another example, which is associated with 4.7 million deaths globally each year and could contribute to 10 million deaths annually by 2050. Increased treatment costs for people with resistant infections amount to $1 trillion every year9. The antibiotic development pipeline has been depleted over time as economic factors render companies’ return on investment lower than that for other drug classes9. These factors include insufficient funding for research and challenging business models, given the short duration of antibiotic treatments and the need to reserve successful upcoming antibiotics as drugs of last resort, to be used after all other options have failed.

Bringing a therapy to market from discovery can take 10–15 years and cost anywhere between $880 million and $2.3 billion10,11. The majority (90%) of drug candidates fail after entering clinical studies, clinical trials and drug-approval processes12. And companies won’t invest if they are unsure whether a drug will be profitable.

In a recent development, consequently, many diseases and conditions have no or few available therapies or only modestly effective options13. What’s needed is a mission-driven strategy to guide scientific capabilities and industry development towards areas of public need by elucidating biological mechanisms and aligning incentives for diseases in which market forces alone are insufficient14.

We propose addressing this misalignment of incentives by reconceptualizing the government’s role in therapeutic advancement through a model of mission-driven PPP. Complementing existing grant-based systems, the model would position the government as a principal investor in select areas of therapeutic development.

Recent findings suggest that the government would thus influence which areas of health and science receive concentrated attention and how successful outcomes are deployed for the public good. Such a model could address specific national needs and global challenges. Here are seven components.

Technicians at work in a pharmaceutical factory.Credit: Getty.

According to recent reports, select disease targets. We propose the establishment of a government-appointed independent advisory body or commission tasked with identifying priority disease targets using transparent, evidence-based criteria, including disease burden, economic cost, scientific readiness and demonstrable market failure. Further criteria to gauge and consider public input into the selection process could be implemented to ensure public trust.

Set up collaborations. A national government, acting alone or as part of an international consortium, would assume a leading role in supporting basic research into biological mechanisms. It would do so by bringing together basic scientists from academia and translational experts from industry to reduce risks in translational development. Private industry would contribute expertise in drug development, clinical trials, regulatory strategy, manufacturing and commercialization.

In a recent development, provide initial investments. The proposed PPP would not replace existing grant-based systems or market-driven innovation; rather, it would act as a complement by targeting disease areas in which market risks and incentives consistently fail to generate sufficient private investment. The approach could yield fresh therapies and reduce the cost of care to society while generating revenue from new products.

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?

Recent findings suggest that in the United States, we propose a federal investment of one billion dollars annually over ten years, directed to specific disease areas. That is less than 1.8% of total US government spending on biomedical research, which was $54.5 billion in 2024. This would be supplemented by smaller investments of 10–20% of one billion dollars from a consortium of philanthropic foundations and industry partners joining the initiative in response to a request for application. Given the high costs of bringing a new drug to market, a $10-billion total investment should provide the scale and time needed to pursue about three major disease targets10–12.

According to recent reports, feed revenues back in. Public return is a defining feature of the PPP. Existing biomedical funding structures are mainly grant making, with the implication that public benefit will emerge indirectly through the downstream health improvements and economic growth spurred by discovery. By contrast, this PPP framework would directly incorporate public accountability as well as returns.

Industry observers note that the government would need to leverage its status as a majority investor to ensure access, fair pricing and affordability. It might require conditions such as agreements to ensure access. Pricing frameworks could incorporate a value-based approach to pricing, in which health insurers offer reimbursements determined by a drug’s value for patients. Affordability conditions, such as reasonable-pricing clauses, would also serve as powerful leverage.

As if having his first training session as Manchester United head coach sabotaged by a drone wasn’t dramatic enough, Mauricio Pochettino’s second day at work saw access to the club’s training base blocked by a serious road accident.

The collision between a vehicle and a cyclist on one of the two approaches to Carrington, where United’s players and staff are regularly seen driving through a security checkpoint, meant it was closed off for several hours on Friday while an ambulance and police cars attended the scene.

Greater Manchester Police say the cyclist was taken to hospital to receive treatment for injuries that were not life-threatening and no arrests were made.

Industry observers note that however, anyone leaving Carrington had to take an alternative route in the opposite direction. That included the players after training and Pochettino and his staff following his first pre-match press conference.

The accident on Friday completed an eventful 48 hours at Carrington after a rogue drone operator filmed 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first training session and posted it on YouTube. He later took the video down and apologised for the intrusion, which United sources said was the right thing to do – even though they had not contacted the uploader directly and do not intend to take legal action against him.

According to recent reports, they insisted there was not a breach of security at Carrington, but claimed a number of laws had been broken. Insiders promised a robust response to any further incidents to protect the rights of the club and its staff, and warned that those responsible would be ‘exposing themselves to significant legal and financial risk’.

It's been a testing first few days for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United boss.

One of the unexpected issues to hamper the Argentine was a drone filming his first training session.

Meanwhile, players leaving Carrington last Friday had to take an alternative route after a serious road accident near United's training ground.

Early start after Anfield mauling.

Confidential understands Pochettino ordered the United players into Carrington an hour early on Monday morning to flush the Liverpool defeat out of their systems as soon as possible.

The squad were pictured arriving around 8.30am as they looked to regroup after the 4-0 hammering at Anfield and begin their preparations for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal on Wednesday night.

The Argentine is eager to spend as much time as possible with the players on the training ground, having only taken over as United boss last Wednesday – four days before the Liverpool clash.

United now face 11 games in 43 days and sources believe there may not be too many days off as Pochettino tries to haul his team out of the relegation zone and ensure qualification for the knockout stage of the Champions League.

At least the indications are that he will allow the players to stay at home the night before games at Old Trafford, rather than having them cooped up in a hotel like some previous United managers.

Pochettino ordered the United players into Carrington an hour early on Monday morning to flush the Liverpool defeat out of their systems.

Matheus Cunha won’t play any part against Sporting following his red card in United's last Champions League tie against Roma three weeks ago.

Confidential has learned the Brazilian was set to claim the player of the match award after scoring two late goals in the 3-2 win over Roma, only for UEFA to step in.

UEFA rules prevent a player who has been sent off from receiving the award and so the selector – in this case Steve Cooper, the former Leicester, Nottingham Forest and Swansea boss who is now one of the governing body's technical observers – was forced into a late switch, picking Bruno Fernandes instead.

According to recent reports, cunha’s absence will be keenly felt in Portugal. He played no part in Tuesday’s training session at Carrington, instead working on his own in the gym.

At a time when United have the most porous defence in Europe’s top five leagues and Matthijs de Ligt, Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez and Ayden Heaven are all struggling for form, Pochettino is going to need Harry Maguire.

Pochettino overlooked the experienced Englishman from the start for the trip to Anfield but ended the match with Maguire on the pitch and he was United’s best defender on another desperate afternoon.

Maguire is walking the tightrope of a ban as he remains on four yellow cards after 11 league games. Players are hit with a one-match ban once they receive five or more yellows prior to the conclusion of the 19th league game of the season – eight matches from now.

Even after Yoro's red card at Anfield was overturned on appeal, Pochettino can ill-afford to be without Maguire going forward.

Pochettino is going to need the experience of Harry Maguire to hold his defence together but he faces a ban if he is booked again.

United are still waiting to see if Pochettino’s strength and conditioning specialist Silvia Tuya can join his staff at Carrington despite hiring new fitness coach Sam Wilson.

Wilson has joined United following his departure from Parma in October, having only moved to the Italian club as head of performance in the summer after 12 years at Arsenal.

It is understood Tuya has not yet been confirmed as part of Pochettino’s backroom team because she is waiting to see if a work permit will be approved.

She joined the US national team staff in October 2024 shortly after Pochettino, and travelled with him, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino and analyst Alec Scott when they flew from Cincinnati to Manchester by private jet last week.

Strength and conditioning specialist Silvia Tuya has not yet been confirmed as part of Pochettino’s backroom team.

It has been revealed that some of the early changes under Pochettino have been more subtle than others. Observant fans may have noticed that when the club announced the team to face Liverpool at 3.15pm on Sunday, it was in positional order.

Recent findings suggest that previously, United’s line-up has been listed numerically, leaving fans to deliberate over the formation. But Pochettino liked to name his team positionally at Tottenham and Chelsea, and admitted in a Q&A on MUTV last week that he wants to do the same at United.

It was clear from the club’s social media post on Sunday that Pochettino would be sticking to the 4-3-2-1 formation favoured by Michael Carrick, with Patrick Dorgu returning on the left wing and Cunha leading the attack.

Not that it lasted very long, as Pochettino admitted he was forced to put his game blueprint ‘in the bin’ inside eight minutes when Yoro was sent off.

This weekend’s match-up between United and Brentford brings together the most ill-disciplined English team in all competitions and the dirtiest team in the Premier League.

No English team has had more players sent off this season than United’s four – Yoro twice, Cunha against Roma and Martinez against Chelsea.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, Brentford are bottom of the Premier League’s disciplinary 'points table' thanks to their three red cards and 22 yellow cards. So expect referee Rob Jones to be a busy man on Pochettino’s home debut.

Leny Yoro brings down Alexander Isak at Anfield and is sent off - his second red card of the season.

Richard Arnold, who preceded Omar Berrada as United's chief executive, pocketed a £5.53m pay-off to stand down after Ineos moved into the club.

While Omar Berrada found himself back in the firing line last weekend, the man he succeeded as United’s chief executive was cutting a much more relaxed figure.

Richard Arnold, who led United between February 2022 and December 2023, was spotted enjoying himself on Chester’s popular Eastgate Street on Saturday night – 24 hours before a beleaguered Berrada watched United’s 4-0 thrashing 30 miles down the road at Anfield.

Industry observers note that after stepping up to replace Ed Woodward, Arnold was in charge of United for the period spanning United’s strategic review which led to Sir Jim Ratcliffe acquiring 29 per cent of the club. Once it became clear that Ineos would take over the day-to-day running of United, he accepted a £5.53million pay-off to stand down, with the club’s general counsel Patrick Stewart stepping in on an interim basis.

Arnold is now enjoying a quieter life as an executive director at Norton Motorcycles and, it would appear, nights out close to his home near Chester.

It was there that he met a group of United protesters outside his local pub in June 2022 and admitted that the last 12 months had been ‘a f****** nightmare’ and United had ‘f****** burned through cash’. Nothing much seems to have changed since then.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

According to recent reports, rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Industry observers note that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

In a recent development, equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

According to recent reports, carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

Recent findings suggest that “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager remarked. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

In a recent development, it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Recent findings suggest that marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

Industry observers note that united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

Recent findings suggest that united fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

In a recent development, it had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

In a recent development, speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick remarked: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

It has been revealed that “We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

Vincenzo Montella’s time with AC Milan was ‘a dream’ for him, but he failed to achieve much during his time at the helm.

Industry observers note that looking back on Montella’s time leading Milan is tricky. On paper, the Italian had a strong tenure at the club, achieving a 50% win rate and only losing 18 of his 64 games in charge at San Siro, not a terrible record by any means.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that he even ended a five-year trophy drought with a win against Juventus in the Supercoppa Italiana and returned the Rossoneri to Europe, with a sixth-place finish in the 2016/17 season. In itself, that was a first since 2014.

This is where context matters, though. The start of the 2017/18 season was tough, as the Diavolo won six of their first 14 games and he was sacked before December. Despite that, he still views the club in an excellent light.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport’s ‘La Tripletta’ podcast, Montella went over his time with the club and how he fulfilled a dream by taking the job, as MilanPress relays.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a fantastic experience there [at Milan] too, it was my dream. Then, as a professional, it’s a little different, but when I was thirteen I was a fan of that AC Milan team. My older brother took me to see Maradona’s Napoli team twice to make me a Napoli fan, and Maradona scored three goals.

Sources indicate that “Despite this, my idol was Van Basten because I was a striker: I studied him and dreamed of becoming like him, and so I was a Milan fan. I knew everything about Milan, so for me it was an incredible feeling to join Milan.”.

It has been revealed that “He liked to talk about football; he liked to give advice even when it was a bit out of context at the time, because he always had the mentality of having Van Basten as a centre forward with Papin, a two-time Ballon d’Or winner, on the bench. He wanted me to play with two strikers, and I tried to plug the gap for months.

Recent findings suggest that “I told him it was difficult; I knew all the lineups of those years. I was a Milan fan: the starter was Van Basten and the reserve was Papin, both Ballon d’Or winners. So, ‘If you buy me some players like that, rest assured that I’ll play them both.'”.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a year when we returned to Europe. I think it had been two or three years since Milan had been there, and it was something latest at the time. We won a trophy, a small one. Just the other night I saw Galliani at a dinner; he reminded me of it and remembers it perfectly.

“I have to say that I found him to be the perfect manager at the time, because he was always on my side when it came to pressure; he gave me complete autonomy in my decisions and he helped me with everything, from the number of collaborators to new things; whatever I asked for, he was always on the coach’s side.

“And so for me he was truly an incredible manager, who in that phase, in that change, was fundamental even in achieving these small results, especially after Berlusconi’s great AC Milan.

Industry observers note that “We deserved to win even in regulation time: we had some easy chances to win it, then it came to penalties. Gigio saved the penalty from Dybala, who kicked it really hard, but he filled the net with it.”.

“I was a little worried from the beginning because there was this obsession with publicising everything, almost like a publicity stunt, so I was a little worried. In theory, there was sharing, at least that’s what it looked like, but I couldn’t back out when in reality that wasn’t always the case.

“And so sometimes there were players I hadn’t even consulted about, who would arrive and then say, ‘It was shared,’ and when you’re there, you can’t say otherwise. Certainly, when you build a team and have the budget, the first thing you do is: we had a goalkeeper, I’ll get a centre forward, we were missing a centre forward.

“In the final selection, the centre forward was the only one left, with a budget of 15-20 million. And then Kalinic… yes, I chose him because that was the final budget. So our, let’s say, second-choice striker was paid thirty-eight million, if I remember correctly, who was André Silva, and the first striker was paid half that.

“And so, in my opinion, a misunderstanding of this kind was created, with so many changes, even though at that stage we weren’t even playing badly for having fifteen upcoming players.

“We still had Calhanoglu, who wasn’t feeling well, coming off months of suspension. The team was still being built: we weren’t in line with the Scudetto objectives that had been announced, but certainly, given our development, we were absolutely on target.

Industry observers note that “Who would I have signed up front? At the time, we were probably negotiating for Aubameyang, if I remember correctly. Ronaldo? No, I didn’t believe it, not at all.”.

Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but they responded to that setback in Istanbul with a thoroughly impressive victory against the Belgian side, with whom they were level on points prior to the match.

That result has left Andoni Iraola’s team fifth in the league phase standings with 12 points from a possible 15, with a top-eight finish seeing them bypass the bear pit of the knockout play-off round in February.

Now that we’re past the halfway mark of the league phase, the 36 Champions League clubs have a strong indication as to where they’re likely to finish, and what more needs to be done to achieve their targets.

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

At present, Manchester City occupy the final position for automatic passage to the round of 16, with Enzo Maresca’s side on 10 points, averaging two per game.

That means the projected points tally required for a top-eight placing is 16, so Liverpool would need to aim for at least four points from their remaining three matches against Porto (home), Inter Milan (away) and Lens (home).

The two Anfield fixtures are against teams placed 22nd and 34th respectively, so the Reds would be fully expected to win both of those.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

The visit to the San Siro is likely to be much tougher, but LFC beat Inter at the famous venue last season, and a repeat result would probably be enough to guarantee a top-eight finish with one game to spare.

That’d give Iraola the luxury of being able to rest key players for the concluding fixture against Lens, which falls between Premier League matches against Manchester United and Everton.

With Liverpool also still going strong in the Carabao Cup and plausibly making it to a two-legged semi-final in the opening weeks of 2027, any opportunity to rotate the squad in January must be embraced.

The picture can obviously change over the final three matchdays, but right now it seems probable that if the Reds beat Porto and get a result away to Inter, they could be effectively or even mathematically assured of a top-eight finish by the time they host Lens.

That objective is well within reach for Iraola’s side, and avoiding the play-off round in February is a must.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 26 Nov 2026 11:46, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 11:48.

Palmeiras and Estudiantes meet on Saturday afternoon in the 2026 Copa Libertadores final.

The clash at the iconic Estadio Centenario revives memories of the 1968 final, when Estudiantes claimed the first of their four titles and became the first Argentine side to beat a Brazilian team in the final.

Palmeiras, meanwhile, are chasing a fourth continental title after reaching three of the last six finals.

After 58 years, Palmeiras have the chance to renew their rivalry with Estudiantes in a final worthy of the occasion. The 1968 final was decided over three matches: the Argentines won the first leg in La Plata before losing at the old Pacaembu.

It has been revealed that in the decider at the same Estadio Centenario, Estudiantes won 2-0, with goals from Ribaudo and Juan Ramon Veron. One of the goals in Estudiantes’ first Libertadores triumph was scored by the father of the club’s current president, Juan Sebastian Veron.

In a recent development, palmeiras have not been as dominant in 2026 as in previous years. They drew two of their six group-stage matches, but have taken the lead in eight of their last 10 continental fixtures during the knockout rounds.

In the round of 16, the Alviverde gained revenge on Cerro Porteno, completing a quartet of meetings between the sides this campaign.

Sources indicate that abel Ferreira's men then needed penalties to overcome LDU Quito in the quarter-finals and Fluminense in the semi-finals. Goalkeeper Carlos Miguel proved crucial on both occasions, making three saves in total.

After losing the national title to Flamengo last Saturday, Palmeiras fielded a reserve side in Tuesday’s visit to Chapecoense and suffered a 3-0 defeat.

In a recent development, although the result did not change their position in the Brasileiro table, Palmeiras are now winless in four matches across all competitions. They have also conceded in each of their last five outings.

Like Palmeiras, Estudiantes have also faced the same opponent four times in this edition: Flamengo, the reigning continental champions and two-time Brazilian champions.

Industry observers note that in Group A, Alexander Medina's men suffered a narrow defeat at the Maracana and drew 1-1 at the Jorge Luis Hirschi. In the semi-finals, the Pincha held the favourites to two goalless draws before goalkeeper Fernando Muslera starred in the shootout, saving penalties from Jorginho, Lucas Paqueta, and Bruno Henrique.

That trademark Argentine resilience was also evident against Universidad Catolica in Chile, and especially across the two quarter-final matches against Corinthians.

Recent findings suggest that estudiantes have conceded an average of just 0.5 goals per match across their last 10 Libertadores games. Since the round of 16, Muslera has been beaten only twice.

Their main concern is at the other end: Estudiantes have scored no more than once in nine of their last 10 matches in the tournament. A closely fought contest in Montevideo could therefore be in prospect.

According to recent reports, forward Paulinho is also a major doubt after developing inflammation in the muscle and bone tissue in his calf. Even if he recovers, he could miss the Copa do Brasil final.

Uruguay international full-back Joaquin Piquerez was rested against Rubro-Negro but is expected to return on the left in his home country.

With the usual recovery period around three weeks, the former Botafogo forward is undergoing intensive treatment in a bid to make the bench.
