📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 24 November 2026.

Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

Nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

Recent findings suggest that but the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17.

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany.

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

Recent findings suggest that well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a massive amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he noted.

In a recent development, ‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’.

Recent findings suggest that there's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a initiative to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ says Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

According to recent reports, ‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’.

'He lacks confidence and I think that indicates in his play,' claims Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri.

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week.

Nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against Newly introduced Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

According to recent reports, to make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

Industry observers note that wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that indicates in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

Sources indicate that ‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’.

Recent findings suggest that there is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

Recent findings suggest that in any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Female mosquitoes use several sensory systems to locate a host whose blood they can feed on.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Female mosquitoes use several sensory systems to locate a host whose blood they can feed on. One of these systems is a group of proteins known as ionotropic receptors, which detect the acidic compounds in human sweat that contribute to its sour smell. Writing in Nature, Xu et al.1 report 3D structures of an ionotropic-receptor complex from the malaria-spreading mosquito Anopheles stephensi. The structures show how the binding of an acid activates the receptor, which then opens its ion-conducting pore and generates an electrical signal that helps to guide the mosquito towards a human host.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 11:46.

Aiming to move themselves back into the top half of the Championship, struggling West Ham United welcome promotion-chasing Stoke City to the London Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The Hammers' woeful run of form continued at the Fratton Park base of Portsmouth earlier in the week, whilst the Potters picked up yet another Staffordshire victory, this time at the expense of Millwall.

Back in the Championship for the first time since 2012, West Ham United were expected by many to sit at the top of the rankings and waltz to a Premier League return, however, the East Londoners hit a new low on Tuesday night.

The Hammers extended their winless run to a worrying six matches (D2 L4) at Fratton Park, where a first-half effort from Odin Bailey was enough for Portsmouth victory, with the visitors once again failing to break down a stubborn second-tier defence.

Since the early-November arrival of Scott Parker to the managerial hotseat, West Ham have collected just two points across a quartet of fixtures, dropping down to 13th spot in the Championship table - a staggering 11 points behind first-placed Middlesbrough.

Following three away matches in their past four, the Hammers are back at their London Stadium base on Saturday, when Parker's men will be looking to halt a five-game winless run (D2 L3) at the East London venue.

In fact, West Ham rank 17th in terms of home form so far this season, with the pre-season title favourites last picking up three points in front of their own supporters on September 11, when Wrexham were hit for six without reply.

After placing between 16th and 18th in each of the past four Championship seasons, Stoke City have swapped midtable mediocrity for a Premier League chase in 2026-27, winning 11 of their past 14 league fixtures.

The in-form Potters have now gone seven games (W6 D1) without defeat after Wednesday night's impressive showing against Millwall, with George Hirst grabbing the headlines once again courtesy of a game-winning brace.

After recording five consecutive league victories for the first time since the days of Tony Pulis in February 2008, Stoke have moved up to second spot in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Middlesbrough.

The Staffordshire side managed just six league wins on the road last season but could equal that tally already with success this weekend at the London Stadium, where the Potters last played in April 2018.

That East London clash represents the most recent meeting between West Ham and Stoke, with a 90th-minute leveller from towering striker Andy Carroll forcing a share of the spoils following Peter Crouch's opener.

West Ham United Championship form:.

Looking for his first victory as West Ham boss at the fifth attempt, head coach Parker could make changes from the side that was defeated by Portsmouth.

However, there is little room for manoeuvre at right-back, where Joel Veltman should start in the absence of Kyle Walker-Peters (muscle).

Young goalkeeper Finlay Herrick could play once again, with Danish stopper Mads Hermansen dropped to the bench for the past two games.

Stoke suffered a major injury blow during the win over Birmingham City last weekend, with Djibril Soumare picking up a muscular injury.

In the absence of the influential midfielder, Jack McGlynn could start in a deeper role alongside fellow summer arrival Ethan Galbraith.

West Ham United possible starting lineup:.

Herrick; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Soucek; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa, Solomon; Piroe.

Stoke City possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, McGlynn, Galbraith, Devenny; Manhoef, Bae, Hirst.

Without a victory under newly introduced boss Parker, West Ham's ambitions of an instant Premier League return are fading swiftly.

Stoke will be in the mood to take full advantage of a Hammers side devoid of confidence, however, we feel that a share of the points is forthcoming at the London Stadium.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered.
  • How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.
  • It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

Industry observers note that this is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

It has been revealed that there was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k.

The midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

Sources indicate that this is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

Instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

They are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

According to recent reports, in the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other major signings to respond.

But this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. He was lightweight and so, ultimately, were Liverpool.

Erling Haaland gives Manchester City the lead against Liverpool 🎯 https://t.co/cELo5y60Fk.

In fact, Liverpool’s best performers were the young attackers Victor Muñoz and, making his first league start as a makeshift centre-forward, Lewis Koumas, who is just 21. Against that, City unleashed a battery of forward talent.

"Koumas & Munoz were better than the two £100million players!" Jamie Carragher is still disappointed with what he's seeing from Florian Wirtz in a Liverpool shirt 😬🔴 https://t.co/jJwOZbPJ4b.

Was it an unfair advantage? It appears City have been thriving off that for some time and, while this team were not signed during the years the club have been found guilty of cheating, the argument is, of course, that they would not have joined without the sporting supremacy.

Industry observers note that certainly not Haaland, despite his avowed love for City. That cannot be doubted as his father, Alf-Inge, a former midfielder for the club, stood celebrating in the away end. The striker missed one chance when he should have scored, sent through on goal, shaking his head in disbelief at getting his angles wrong. “One hundred per cent… Because I know the organisation from years ago, and I know how serious they are, I know that they do the right things. I would like to speak about this when we win the appeal.”.

While Liverpool have struggled for wins in this fixture of late, it’s worth noting that this run includes five draws.

Liverpool have won just three of their last 13 Premier League clashes with Man City 👀 https://t.co/OxkeDpLjQq.

On Saturday Manchester United fans resurrected their “ticker” mocking Manchester City’s trophy drought following their rivals’ cheating scandal:.

There was also a nod to Rui Pinto, the whistleblower whose Football Leaks documents prompted the Premier League’s investigation into City:.

There were four days between the news leaking that Manchester City had been found guilty of the majority of charges first levelled at them by the Premier League in February 2023 and the independent commission findings dropping.

Staff, then, had had a bit of time to process a guilty verdict although little, it seems, could adequately prepare them for the excoriating tone and content of the commission’s ruling.

“The thing that has shocked me more than anything is the language the commission used to describe the club’s conduct,” one staff member told Telegraph Sport this week.

Industry observers note that “We had been waiting for a very long time to see what came out of these Premier League charges and lots of different things go through your head. But I just wasn’t expecting that. I’m still a bit shell-shocked by the ferocity of what the commission noted. I think that’s what’s worried me.”.

"Enjoy the ride and smile" Erling Haaland with a message for Man City fans ahead of their trip to Anfield this weekend 🎙️🩵 https://t.co/H7so0fk6XE.

“The international break is good because we can review what we have done and what we can do better,” Enzo Maresca said after Manchester City’s harum-scarum 5-3 victory over Sunderland. “But at the same time we can relax a little bit more.” One wonders how much respite Enzo Maresca and Manchester City actually enjoyed in the intervening 21 days.

Sources indicate that since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. Until then, though, the show goes on and City’s players and staff must compete knowing that their every move now comes with a caveat.

City have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca noted, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

Given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

Alisson Becker made Champions League history in Liverpool’s 3-0 win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds’ number 1 didn’t have his best outing in his previous European game, committing a costly error in the 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but he’s been in terrific form since that aberration in Istanbul.

He gave one of his best-ever performances in the recent victory at Crystal Palace and has followed that up with consecutive clean sheets against Manchester United and Club Brugge.

Not only did he achieve a shutout in Belgium, he also claimed an assist for Alexander Isak’s second goal, with his long kickout finding the Swedish striker, who shrugged off the challenge of Brandon Mechele before finishing neatly past Yann Sommer.

As noted by liverpoolfc.com, Alisson became the first Liverpool goalkeeper to record an assist in the Champions League, with that being the fourth goal he’s set up during his time with the Reds.

It also puts him level with Pepe Reina and Bruce Grobbelaar for assists with LFC, and the Brazilian has achieved it in fewer games than those two.

Industry observers note that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Liverpool fans are no strangers to seeing their number 1 set up an attacking teammate to score, having done so for Mo Salah on three occasions, including the memorable clincher at home to Man United in January 2020.

We’ve even been fortunate enough to see Alisson get on the scoresheet himself with that famous stoppage-time winner against West Brom in May 2021 when Champions League qualification was in the balance.

The assist for Isak was a nice bonus to go along with another strong outing in terms of his core goalkeeping duties, having pulled off a terrific save to deny Felix Lemarechal when the score was 1-0 in the second half and Club Brugge were pushing hard for an equaliser.

As it stands, this’ll be the Brazilian’s final season as a Liverpool player, with his current contract due to expire next June, although his agent is reportedly in talks with club chiefs over a prospective extension.

Considering his ongoing importance to the Reds, we hope and pray that Alisson (still only 34) will agree to stay on for at least another year or two – possibly time enough for him to add more assists to his tally!

Published: 09:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 24 November 2026.

They had a World Cup winner in defence, Superman in their squad and a Sex Pistol in charge of recruitment.

There's a clue in the name, but Hollywood United must have been the wildest, most star-studded pub football team of all time.

Ray Winstone, Jason Statham, Mike Myers and Vinnie Jones all turned out for a team that grew out of a gathering of British expats at the Cat & Fiddle pub in the late Eighties.

It being Hollywood, they travelled to matches by private jet and they even took on David Beckham in a charity match.

Now, as the Sex Pistols prepare to embark on a tour marking the 50th anniversary of their debut single, guitarist Steve Jones has revealed how he assembled the extraordinary side on Hollywood's Sunset Boulevard.

Among those who pulled on the shirt were France's World Cup-winning defender Frank Leboeuf, former Scotland captain Richard Gough and Brandon Routh, the American actor who played the superhero in the 2006 film Superman Returns.

Routh was given no special treatment by his team-mates, who would mockingly shout ‘Superman!’ whenever he made a mistake.

Hollywood United is the world's most famous pub team - featuring a littany of high-profile stars.

Created by British expat and Sex Pistols star Steve Jones (right), United have rubbed shoulders with the likes of David Beckham.

Vinnie Jones, meanwhile, had apparently lost none of the competitive instincts that characterised his career in English football.

In 2002, it was reported that he had been sent off just 15 seconds after coming on as a substitute in a Hollywood United friendly.

Anthony LaPaglia, the Australian actor who starred in the hit television series Without a Trace, was their goalkeeper.

There were members of the Sex Pistols, The Cult and Def Leppard, as well as actors such as Ralf Little.

But there were also rather less celebrated footballers.

‘The start of it was with me and Anthony LaPaglia; he was a goalie, and from there it turned into Hollywood United,’ Jones told the Telegraph.

‘We always used to play in a league with a bunch of regular blokes, carpenters and so on, then we got a few more faces who wanted to start kicking about with us like Vinnie Jones.’.

The two Joneses met in a video shop in Los Angeles and the former Wimbledon hardman, who had embarked on a film career with Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, needed little persuasion to join.

According to recent reports, ‘He was up for a laugh, and he knows where to put a ball. Most of the team were amateurs, but we were decent and reached a certain level.’.

In November 2007, Hollywood United took on Beckham's LA Galaxy in a charity match.

According to recent reports, england manager Steve McClaren had flown to California to assess Beckham's fitness ahead of a European Championship qualifier against Croatia. It's not clear whether he attended the match, which Hollywood United lost 12-4. Beckham scored twice, as did Leboeuf and over 5,000 spectators raised more than $100,000 for victims of the California wildfires.

Steve Jones, now 71, had himself broken one of football's golden rules by changing his allegiance.

Vinnie Jones (left) and Ray Winstone (right) have turned out for the amateur football team.

Actor Anthony LaPaglia lets the team travel on his private jet to matches across America.

Having followed QPR as a schoolboy in west London and also been associated with Fulham, he became a Chelsea supporter after moving to California and getting sober.

Chelsea's games were available on American television and his lifelong friend and fellow Sex Pistol Paul Cook was already a diehard Blues fan.

Hollywood United played at Griffith Park, beneath the famous Hollywood sign, but their adventures would take them considerably further afield.

LaPaglia would arrange private jets to transport the players to matches.

Gough recalls one trip when the team flew to Vancouver for a charity match before heading straight to the Mexican resort of Puerto Vallarta to play a side of former Mexico internationals.

Vinnie Jones also told the Guardian in 2007 that Hollywood United had fielded nine former international footballers in a single match.

The club's ranks included former Liverpool and Newcastle defender Barry Venison and United States internationals Alexi Lalas and Eric Wynalda.

Winstone, a lifelong West Ham fan, found playing in the Californian heat rather more demanding than he had anticipated.

According to recent reports, he later recalled being so exhausted by the time the ball reached him that he was barely able to kick it. And he wasn't particularly impressed by the willingness of former Chelsea defender Leboeuf to pass the ball, describing the Frenchman as a greedy player.

Among those watching from the touchline was the actor John Hurt, who was in town filming Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull with Winstone.

Some of the rock stars had impressive footballing pedigrees.

Ian Astbury, the lead singer of The Cult, had played boys' club football in Glasgow alongside future Everton and Scotland striker Graeme Sharp.

Gough, meanwhile, struck up a conversation with a team-mate from Northern Ireland without having the slightest idea he was Vivian Campbell, the guitarist of Def Leppard.

Sex Pistol Jones, who has lived in Los Angeles for more than 40 years, is returning to Britain next month for a tour marking the 50th anniversary of the release of Anarchy in the UK.

He still regularly attends football matches whenever he is back in England, although he has little time for the corporate hospitality enjoyed by many of his celebrity contemporaries.

‘I don't care where I sit, but I'm not interested in sitting in some box with a bunch of t***ers.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 12:11, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 12:20.

Meeting for the first time in their history, League One newcomers Bromley will be looking to climb out of the relegation zone when they welcome Burton Albion to Hayes Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Ravens will be aiming to make it three league matches unbeaten after following up a win over Reading with a home draw against Wycombe Wanderers on Tuesday night, while the Brewers will be hoping to end their three-game losing streak after suffering a 2-1 defeat to an in-form Luton Town side last Saturday.

After securing promotion to the third tier for the first time in their history last May under the stewardship of long-serving manager Andy Woodman, Bromley were expected to face a difficult first season at this level, with the club having every reason to stick by the man who had guided them to two promotions in three seasons and taken them from the National League to League One.

However, Woodman's five-and-a-half-year spell at the club came to an abrupt end in late October after a 4-0 defeat to Leicester City left the Ravens 23rd in the table following 10 matches, a decision that came as a surprise and disappointment to many Bromley supporters.

The London-based side turned to former MK Dons, Charlton Athletic, Oxford United and Salford City boss Karl Robinson, who will take charge of his fifth match as Bromley manager this weekend.

Robinson's arrival was followed by exits from both the FA Cup and EFL Trophy in his opening two matches, but he has since managed to steady the ship in the league, guiding his side to a narrow victory over Reading before they followed that up with a draw at home to Wycombe Wanderers during the week, leaving him unbeaten in League One since taking charge.

Those four points from their last two outings have provided some much-needed momentum ahead of a busy festive period, although Bromley remain in the bottom four with 13 points to their name, meaning a fourth league victory of the season could be enough to lift the Ravens out of the relegation zone ahead of the final month of the calendar year.

As for Burton Albion, they make the journey to Greater London from Staffordshire hoping to bring an end to a three-match losing streak in League One that has seen them slip out of the top half and move dangerously close to the relegation places.

A victory in their final home fixture of October against Leyton Orient was followed by defeats to Wycombe Wanderers, MK Dons and, most recently, Luton Town, with the second of those losses proving particularly damaging as they were beaten 6-2 at Stadium MK.

The Halloween defeat to the Chairboys was at least followed by a 4-0 FA Cup victory over AFC Rushden and Diamonds at the start of November, but that remains Burton's only win in their last five matches across all competitions, a run that has also included a defeat to Notts County in the EFL Trophy.

Although their heavy loss to MK Dons came against an in-form side, Burton's own defensive record has taken a significant hit, with Gary Bowyer's men now having conceded 29 goals in their 16 League One outings, a tally bettered only by their upcoming opponents.

With that stated, only two teams in the bottom half of the table have scored more than the Brewers, highlighting that Bowyer's side have an attacking foundation to build on if they can turn their fortunes around sooner rather than later.

A victory in their first-ever meeting with Bromley could lift Burton as high as 15th and give them a seven-point cushion over the League One relegation zone.

Bromley form (all competitions):.

Burton Albion form (all competitions):.

Having collected four points from his opening two league matches in charge of Bromley, Robinson will be keen to maintain some consistency ahead of the weekend fixture, and he has the option of keeping the same side after coming through Tuesday's draw without any further injury concerns.

Defender Kamarl Grant scored their only goal last time out and could partner makeshift centre-back George Saville once again, unless former West Ham United and Augsburg defender Reece Oxford is ready to make his second appearance of the season after featuring against Reading in what was his first competitive outing in more than four years.

Robinson's relationship with Ravens winger Jodi Jones is reportedly strained following events during their time at previous clubs, and the former Notts County attacker is expected to remain on the bench for this encounter.

As for Burton, they are likely to be forced into a change after Joe Lewis was forced off with an injury late in their defeat to Luton, with the defender expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Jason Sraha.

Lewis is set to join several teammates in the treatment room, with Finn Delap, George Evans, Kyran Lofthouse and Caylan Vickers also expected to remain sidelined due to various injury and fitness concerns, leaving the Brewers unable to fill their matchday squad in recent weeks.

Matthew Dennis, however, returned to the team after missing just one fixture and could come back into the starting lineup to lead the line, potentially at the expense of either Mark O'Mahony or Gbemi Arubi.

Emeka Adeile has started just two league matches all season but has scored in consecutive appearances and is expected to retain his place out wide on Saturday afternoon.

Bromley possible starting lineup:.

George; Ifill, Grant, Oxford, Mendy; Pinnock, McKiernan, Conteh, Archer; Whitely, Adeboyejo.

Burton Albion possible starting lineup:.

Addai; Sibbick, Sraha, Tilt; Rodrigues, Chauke, Krubally, Adeile; Collar; O'Mahony, Dennis.

With both sides heading into December embroiled in an unwanted battle near the bottom of the table, they will be eager to pick up valuable points, move further clear of danger and build some much-needed momentum.

We expect the pair to play out a 1-1 draw, allowing Robinson to maintain his unbeaten start to life as Bromley manager in League One.

Possible punishments have ranged from points deductions to the stripping of titles, even to expulsion all the way to the National League.

King is already concerned that the Citizens' punishment could be reduced, and he's now outlined why that might be based on the long wait.

When discussing Man City's legal battle, King told Football Insider: "There's not a full guilty or not guilty decision made on it. And that's what worries me.

Recent findings suggest that "This has not only become a football thing; this has become a political thing, I'm pretty sure of it. Think how much money the guy who owns Manchester City has invested in the Premier League and the British government.

"No other club, apart from maybe Newcastle, have got the kind of money to invest in the Premier League or a Premier League club like the owners of Newcastle and Manchester City have got.

"None of the American owners... They haven't got this kind of money. You're talking banks and banks here. And that Middle East bank has got a lot of money.

"And I believe that the investment that these banks and these people, who own the football clubs, have made in Great Britain is probably far greater than the money they put in their Premier League football clubs.

Sources indicate that "So, what would happen if they withdrew their funds from the British government? It would hurt the British government more than it would hurt Manchester City and Newcastle.".

With everything going on behind the scenes, performances on the pitch appear to have taken a heavy hit.

Man City have won just one of their last seven matches across all competitions, most recently drawing 2-2 with Napoli at the Etihad.

Mick Brown told Football Insider that alarm bells are already ringing over Enzo Maresca's future, just 19 games into his tenure.

The likes of Nico O'Reilly, Marc Guehi, Phil Foden and even Erling Haaland appear to be suffering on the pitch, and that could be to do with the distractions off it.

Called 'Progressive Actions' it highlights the passes and ball carries that drive a team up the pitch, and the often-unsung players behind them. Developed by Prime Video's team of producers, engineers, AI experts, and on-air analysts, Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built specifically for the UEFA Champions League. It joins the growing suite of features on Prime Vision, the alternate feed which serves as a laboratory and incubator for new features that often advance to the main broadcast.

Sources indicate that progressive Actions is built on proprietary AI-powered models that identify a Progressive Action based on how far the ball travels in each phase of the pitch, with the threshold becoming shorter closer to the opposition goal where defences are more compact and space is harder to find. The metric mirrors the data used behind the scenes at Europe's elite clubs, yet has historically been difficult to show during a live broadcast. As a player makes a Progressive Action, an on-pitch graphic will show where the action started and ended, the player involved, and the distance the ball advanced, allowing fans to see the game as a coaching team would, in real time.

'Prime Vision is where we develop newly introduced features that shine a spotlight on the metrics, actions and players that impact a game most, yet aren't always captured by traditional statistics or broadcast techniques,' noted Andrew Hornett, Director of Live Sports Production for Europe at Prime Video.

Fans will see them in real time as they happen, but we'll also aggregate the data across the game, so you can see which players have had the biggest impact on the match.'.

The feature will debut in the UK and Ireland on Tuesday and will also be available for fans in Germany and Italy. Fans can access Prime Vision, with features including Progressive Actions, via their remote from the match detail page or the in-game menu during any live UCL fixture on Prime Video.

Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built from the ground up specifically for Prime Video's UEFA Champions League coverage, and sits alongside Tactical Map, Momentum, Physical Insights, Advanced Analytics, Passing Options, and Player ID in Prime Vision's growing suite of features designed to take football fans closer to the game, all available on the alternate feed during every UEFA Champions League match live on Prime Video. Prime Insights were first developed for Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football, its exclusive weekly NFL package in the US, where AI-powered features including the award-winning Defensive Alerts have become a staple of the coverage, advancing from the alternate feed to the main broadcast each week.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, he explained how Berrada’s recent comments regarding the squad haven’t helped the manager at all.

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (948 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up.
  • Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins.
  • He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Accurately predicting protein structures has been the preserve of specialist AI tools like AlphaFold — but now general-purpose models are catching up. Credit: EMBL-EBI (CC0).

Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, Xinming Tu set out to test what artificial-intelligence models know about proteins. Tu, a researcher at an AI biology tech giant called Phylo in South San Francisco, California, asked large language models (LLMs) from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google to predict the sequences of obscure bacterial proteins.

He left the analysis to run overnight and woke up shocked at the results. The latest versions of Anthropic’s Claude models had outperformed other LLMs — but also specialized ‘protein language models’, which are trained on vast troves of sequence data and specially designed for such tasks.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary newly introduced proteins.

Scientists are using AI to dream up revolutionary fresh proteins.

When Tu and Leo Chen, a computational biologist at Harvard Medical School in Boston, Massachusetts, shared the results in a 16 November blogpost, it set off a frenzy among computational biologists to see what other protein biology LLMs such as Claude could do. For instance, Tu and Chen and others have found it could perform a key step in protein-structure prediction.

It has been revealed that and on 24 November, OpenAI announced that its latest language models had successfully designed newly introduced proteins, some of which behaved as expected when made and tested in the lab. The results hint that the latest LLMs might be gaining a sophisticated understanding of protein biology.

Sources indicate that the research has kicked off a debate over the future of biological AI. Some scientists predict that ‘general purpose’ models such as Claude and ChatGPT will eventually outperform specialist tools such as AlphaFold at tasks including protein structure prediction and design.

“We want to see a world where a scientist can just describe in natural language what they want a ChatGPT model to do, and the model can just be infinitely flexible and design exactly what the person wants,” notes Joy Jiao, who leads life-sciences research at OpenAI in San Francisco, California.

Sources indicate that but some researchers question the extent to which LLMs are learning underlying lessons in protein biology. They suggest that some of their abilities could be the result of regurgitating training data.

It has been revealed that the release of AlphaFold2, Google DeepMind’s blockbuster protein-structure-prediction AI, in 2020 rolled out a revolution in biological AI. There is now a vast ecosystem of software — much of it open source — for modelling different properties of proteins, such as how they interact with possible drugs, and for designing latest proteins.

Researchers have begun using LLMs to orchestrate these specialist models, but it has mostly been as a time-saving measure, says Martin Pačesa, a structural biologist at the University of Zurich. “In most cases, a specialist will always perform better than a generalist for a given task,” he says.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

Five protein-design questions that still challenge AI.

Sources indicate that to see if an LLM could stand in for specialist protein-design tools, Jiao and her colleagues asked an OpenAI model called GPT-6.2 to design 3D protein structures capable of binding to five different biological targets, including proteins implicated in cancer and immune disorders. After the LLMs generated the designs, the researchers used a specialist AI tool to determine a corresponding genetic sequence. Lab experiments confirmed that around 11% of designs were able to bind their target.

Recent findings suggest that in other experiments, the OpenAI team showed that its LLMs could design protein sequences, redesign existing antibodies, and other tasks typically performed by specialist tools. In some cases, the LLM performed as well as some specialist tools, and in others, such as predicting the 3D structure of proteins, it was far off. OpenAI researchers describe the work in a blogpost and technical paper.

Sources indicate that jiao emphasizes that the work is a proof of principle, and that specialized AI tools were still needed for key steps. Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

In a recent development, matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

It has been revealed that “It was an outstanding performance,” the manager stated. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

Recent findings suggest that the win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

Industry observers note that as for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

It has been revealed that jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the latest arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV.

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Industry observers note that newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR.

It should have been three. Again Wissa was partly to blame, losing the ball in midfield to set Coventry on the counter-attack. When Botman made a mess of a clearance it spun perfectly into the path of Cherif. The net should have bulged but the £20m summer signing from Fenerbahce scuffed wide.

The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE.

Industry observers note that in a flash the balance of play shifted in Newcastle’s favour. They poured forward in search of the equaliser. Jaissle switched to a 4-4-2 with Will Osula joining Fernandez-Pardo up front, but instead of pulling level, Coventry pulled further ahead.

"We need to improve the things we can control, and right now that's a lot" 🗣️ Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle expresses his disappointment after his side's loss to Coventry 👇 https://t.co/fatJkZYyRM.

Very, very satisfying. It’s so hard to win. We played like the team we want to be here. A team you look at and go there’s so much energy and spirit in the group. We know we are going to have to suffer this season, when we don’t have a lot of the ball. We have to understand it. The level is what it is.

The work ethic, the belief. You get what you deserve. Great finishes. We haven’t quite had the rub of the green this season and that might have helped us nick a couple of more points. I’m a firm believer that you keep going. It was a complete performance. We’ve got to keep our feet on the ground because we’re going to have to do 30+ of those but it’s a great feeling for the players.

[Cherif] is very, very exciting because he is so young. He has got a really good manner. He wants to train, he wants to learn. He’s quite quiet but on the pitch he shows a lot of personality. When you see the quality of the strike and the hold-up play, there’s a lot to come from him.

It was good to get a win. We worked very hard for it. It’s so hard to get wins, especially on the road. And now we’re back at home and we have to work on those attributes [that earned us the win] at Forest. We rotated pretty well, there are different aspects of the game we want to improve on regardless of shape.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

The 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

Industry observers note that when Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline states. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Recent findings suggest that today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Recent findings suggest that frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

By Matthew Cooper | 26 Nov 2026 12:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:12.

Peterborough United will be looking to pick up an important victory when they welcome rivals Cambridge United to the Weston Homes Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts at the moment sit 22nd in the League One table, while the visitors are 11th.

Peterborough head into this local derby after ending a four-match winless run last weekend when they beat promotion chasers Plymouth Argyle 2-0.

Harry Ashfield opened the scoring in the first half, before Harry Leonard converted a penalty in stoppage-time to secure all three points.

The win was a welcome boost for Robbie Savage's side, who are fighting for survival and remain in the relegation zone with 13 points from 14 games.

However, they will be looking to carry the momentum of last weekend's win into Saturday's clash, with the Posh targeting back-to-back league victories for the first time since February.

It is also worth noting that Peterborough have a strong recent record against their rivals, having won their last five meetings across all competitions.

Cambridge, meanwhile, are without a win in their last five league games and suffered a disappointing 3-0 home defeat to league leaders Stockport County last Saturday.

Ollie Norwood broke the deadlock early in the second half with a stunning free kick, before Ethan Ennis doubled their lead and Gassan Ahadme scored an unfortunate own goal.

The defeat leaves the U's 11th with 21 points from 15 matches, having suffered just one defeat in their first 10 games before going five without a win.

Head coach Neil Harris has admitted his side have not been "tough to play against" in recent weeks and is keen for them to "get back to being that team".

Peterborough could welcome back Ben Woods and Luca Mendonca on Saturday, but they are both unlikely to start even if they are fit.

Savage is expected to keep faith with the team that beat Plymouth last weekend, with Leonard set to lead the line with support out wide from Bolu Shofowoke and Owura Edwards.

Cambridge may be forced to make at least one change, with the availability of Kelland Watts in doubt after he was forced off against Stockport.

Patrick Bauer could replace Watts in defence, while Louis Appere is set to start up front with support from Zak Bradshaw and Ben Knight.

Peterborough United possible starting lineup:.

Bass; Johnston, Feeney, Hughes, Mills; Jones, Ashfield; Shofowoke, Williams, Edwards; Leonard.

Cambridge United possible starting lineup:.

Eastwood; Perry, Heffernan, Bauer; Bennett, Ball, Mpanzu, Stead; Knight, Bradshaw; Appere.

Peterborough should have renewed confidence after their victory over Plymouth and we are expecting a tight, hard-fought derby clash.

However, today, they’ve been linked to a right-wing back in Marco Palestra.

According to El Nacional, via Football Italia, Chelsea – and more specifically, Xabi Alonso – are looking to sign a new right-sided defender and a move for Jules Kounde is very possible.

Hansi Flick is open to a sale and for €50 million, the Frenchman could move to London.

So, where do the Rossoneri come into this? Well, to help a move, Alonso would be open to letting Palestra leave in the January mercato and there would be no shortage of options.

Indeed, Milan, Juventus and Napoli are all ‘on alert’ to the situation and could make another attempt to sign him. Presumably, a fee would need to be involved if Kounde is coming in for €50m. However, they’d be unlikely to make a profit on the €60m paid for the Italian a few months ago.

Industry observers note that considering they’ve got Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze to come back, as well as Zachary Athekame being on loan. It feels like a strange move for the Rossoneri to potentially make….
